:::{#thm-negate-conditional}
#### Negating a conditional

For [propositions](#def-proposition) $P$ and $Q$,

$$
\neg (P \Rightarrow Q) \equiv P \land \neg Q.
$$

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

By the definition of [implies](#def-implies),
$P \Rightarrow Q$ is false
exactly when $P$ is true and $Q$ is false.
So $\neg (P \Rightarrow Q)$ is true exactly in that row of the [truth table](#def-truth-table).
By the definition of [and](#def-and),
$P \land \neg Q$ is true
exactly when $P$ is true and $\neg Q$ is true.
That is the same row.

:::

:::
